analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The source text introduces three key concepts — בְּחִירָה (free choice/will), אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי (the Jewish person), and עֲבוֹדָה (divine service/work) — none of which appear in bechina-typed edges for this Torah (there are none). The text teaches that: (1) a Jewish person possesses free will over every matter in the world; (2) unlike others who are compelled in certain things, every action an Israelite takes — even traveling to some place — contains avoda (divine service); (3) therefore, free choice applies to everything. The relationships expressed in the text are declarative and definitional, not bechina equivalences. The Rebbe is asserting a theological principle about the scope of free will for Israel, not mapping conceptual parallels between two nodes. No equating language ('הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', 'כַּנַּ"ל') appears. Therefore no additions to packages can be proposed — there are no packages to add to, and no bechina formulations in the source text that would warrant creating new package entries.
